result.title: Artifact-to-Capability: Diagnosing Breaks in Capability Formation of Self-Evolving Agents in a Controlled Environment
result.summary: Self-evolving agents write interaction experience into artifacts and reuse them in later tasks. Most work supports such methods with three proxy signals: artifacts accumulate, behavior changes once they are loaded, and metrics rise. We call this signal-based evaluation. What these signals are meant to indicate, however, has not been defined. To fill this gap, we define capability formation from artifacts as five sequentially dependent properties, two of which form a checkpoint for capability formation, and introduce three-scale diagnosis, which judges these properties at the state, game, and lineage levels. In freestyle Gomoku, Reflexion, Voyager, and DGM evolve with the same base model and all show the three signals, yet each exhibits a distinct capability-formation break. Reflexion shows a legalization gain: its pass rate rises only because more of its moves are legal. Voyager shows a compositional override: components that are sound on their own combine to miss all 20 available one-move wins. DGM shows loss-only drift: after passing the checkpoint, later versions only lose passing states. These counterexamples show that signal-based evaluation cannot determine whether a capability has formed.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在受控五子棋环境中把「从 artifact 到能力形成」拆成五个顺序依赖属性并设检查点，提出状态、对局、谱系三层诊断，用 Reflexion、Voyager、DGM 展示三种不同的能力形成断裂，论证代理信号不足以判定能力是否形成。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「指标上升或行为改变≠机制真正起作用」的诊断框架可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 内容是否被答案实际使用（而非仅靠表面增益或旁路），但研究对象为文本智能体的经验复用，与视觉推理状态无直接联系，需较多核查。
